name: jwt-secret-key
description: The subject method makes an HMAC key for signing or checking JWTs from a secret in config: jjwt's Keys.hmacShaKeyFor, signWith, setSigningKey or verifyWith, Nimbus's MACSigner or MACVerifier, Spring Security's withSecretKey or java-jwt's Algorithm.HMAC256. The value is the first config key the secret comes from; the secret's value is never recorded (ADR 0085).

library.description: The JWT library: jjwt, nimbus-jose-jwt, spring-security or java-jwt.

call.description: The call that takes the secret, such as Keys.hmacShaKeyFor.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the secret comes from, such as app.token.signing.key.

uses.description: What the code of the method's type does with JWTs: sign, verify or both. Absent when it does neither where the extractor sees it.

name: identity-admin-client
description: The subject method builds an identity provider's admin client, Keycloak's (KeycloakBuilder.serverUrl, Keycloak.getInstance). The value is the server's URL as written: a @Value text with its placeholders, which the linker resolves through the unit's config, or a literal URL without credentials (ADR 0085).

product.description: The identity provider, such as Keycloak.

name: jwt-decoder
description: The subject method builds Spring Security's JWT decoder, which checks tokens with an identity provider's keys: NimbusJwtDecoder or NimbusReactiveJwtDecoder withJwkSetUri, withIssuerLocation or withPublicKey, or JwtDecoders and ReactiveJwtDecoders fromIssuerLocation. The value says where the keys come from: jwk-set-uri, issuer or public-key (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

call.description: The call that builds the decoder, such as NimbusJwtDecoder.withJwkSetUri.

url.description: The JWK set's or issuer's URL as written, a @Value text with its placeholders or a literal URL without credentials; absent when the code passes it on from elsewhere.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the URL comes from.

name: http-security
description: The subject sets up how callers sign in or show a token: a method using Spring Security's HttpSecurity or ServerHttpSecurity DSL, or a type annotated with legacy Spring Security OAuth's @EnableAuthorizationServer, @EnableResourceServer, @EnableOAuth2Sso or @EnableOAuth2Client. The value is one of oauth2-login (users sign in through an OAuth2 or OIDC provider), oauth2-resource-server (callers show a provider's token), oauth2-client, oauth2-authorization-server (the subject's unit issues tokens), form-login, http-basic, saml2-login, x509, one-time-token-login or webauthn (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

via.description: HttpSecurity (servlet), ServerHttpSecurity (reactive) or annotation (legacy Spring Security OAuth).

call.description: The DSL call or annotation, such as oauth2Login or @EnableResourceServer.

name: jwt-key-pair
description: The subject method signs or checks JWTs with the key of a key pair: Nimbus's RSASSASigner, RSASSAVerifier, ECDSASigner or ECDSAVerifier. The value is the kind of key, RSA or EC; a key's value is never recorded (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

call.description: The constructor, such as new RSASSASigner.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the key comes from, when the extractor can follow it.

name: identity-client
description: A client that a Keycloak realm export in the subject repository registers: an application that signs users in or gets tokens there. The value is its client ID; its secret is never recorded (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

realm.description: The realm the export is of.

public.description: Whether the client is public (no secret, such as a browser or mobile app).

flows.description: The flows it may use: authorization-code, implicit, password, client-credentials.

pkce.description: The PKCE challenge method it requires, such as S256.

redirectUris.description: Where the provider may send users back to, without credentials.

bearerOnly.description: Present and true when the client only checks tokens and never signs users in (Keycloak's legacy bearer-only clients).

rootUrl.description: The application's root URL as the export gives it, without credentials; it may hold ${ENV} placeholders.

baseUrl.description: The application's base URL as the export gives it, without credentials.

webOrigins.description: The browser origins the provider allows for the client.
